description:
A committed artifact shows that a mutation's wall time is bounded by what it changes, and the repository's testing guide cites evidence that exists.

## Background

The point of the mechanism change is a cost that stops scaling with project history. Two terms carried that scaling, and both are gone by the time this phase runs: the event log rewritten whole on every mutation, and the repository re-read and re-hashed across six capture rounds.

Protection is evidence, not a timing assertion. A wall-clock assertion would be the workspace's first throughput assertion, and the project's position is that elapsed time is the wrong thing to decide a test on. The evidence is a harness run over two builds, including a fixture whose event log is ten times larger with the issue set unchanged, so the log term is isolated from the issue-count term. The guide that cites publication-cost evidence is pinned today to an artifact produced by a harness built around the journal, so it moves to the new artifact in the same phase.

The phase edits the contributor material under `dev/` and `scripts/` and no page of the adopter surface, so the mechanical documentation gate, whose footprint is `docs/`, has nothing to check here.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every quantitative claim in the committed artifact traces to the committed harness, which reproduces it from the stated inputs.
- [hard] REQ-02: The repository's testing guide and benchmark contracts cite only evidence artifacts that exist, produced by harnesses that ship.
- [hard] REQ-03: The suite holds no wall-clock throughput assertion, and no test is held out of the default run to keep one quiet.
- [hard] REQ-04: The epic's cumulative Rust line balance from its base revision removes more lines than it adds, recorded in the artifact.
title: Mutation cost evidence
